extracted.intended_audience: general readers and potential entrants (journalists, authors, composers) interested in Pulitzer Prize rules and history
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, eligibility rules, category criteria, jury/board procedures, and historical notes governing entry and selection for the Pulitzer Prizes across journalism, letters, drama, and music.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry administrative compliance and category fit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pulitzer Prize does not automatically consider all applicable works; entries must specifically be entered and reviewed for administrative compliance by the administrator's staff. Entries must fit in at least one of the specific prize categories, and cannot simply gain entrance for being literary or musical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works are considered only if submitted. Entrants must ensure their work matches a category definition; administrative staff checks compliance. Example: a work cannot be entered merely because it is literary; it must satisfy a category's requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of entry categories per work
rubrics_metrics.description: Works can only be entered in a maximum of two relevant categories, regardless of their properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should pick up to two categories that best match the work; entering in more than two is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship and publication requirements for Book, Drama, and Music categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently, entrants in the Book, Drama and Music categories must be United States citizens, permanent residents of the United States or those who otherwise consider the United States to be their longtime primary home; however, eligible work must be published by United States-based entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure author/creator meets U.S. residency/citizenship/home-country-home-longterm criteria and that publisher/producer is U.S.-based for these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism categories publication eligibility (no nationality restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants to the Journalism categories are not restricted by nationality, provided their submitted work appeared in a United States-based publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign nationals may be eligible for journalism prizes if their reporting was published by a U.S.-based newspaper, magazine, news website or news organization that publishes regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible outlets and online content for journalism entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports and photographs by United States–based newspapers, magazines and news organizations (including news websites) that '[publish] regularly' are eligible for the journalism prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online elements were permitted in all journalism categories except photography beginning in 2007; in December 2008 online-only news sources were considered; magazine eligibility was expanded progressively (2015–2016) and by 2016 applied to all journalism categories. Entrants should confirm current Plan of Award for permitted online formats and eligible outlet types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography entry media restriction (historical note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photography categories historically restricted entries to still images (the two photography categories continued to restrict entries to still images when online elements were first permitted in other journalism categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants to photography categories must submit still images (though rules have evolved; verify current Plan of Award).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury selection and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year, more than 100 jurors are selected by the Pulitzer Prize Board to serve on 22 separate juries for the 23 award categories; most juries consist of five members, except for those for Public Service, Investigative Reporting, Explanatory Reporting, Feature Writing, Commentary and Audio Reporting categories, which have seven members; all book juries have five members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jury membership is chosen by the Board annually; entrants do not select jurors. Jury size varies by category to reflect workload/complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination procedure (three nominations per category)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each award category, a jury makes three nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juries submit a slate of three nominated finalists to the Pulitzer Prize Board; these nominees are publicly announced (names of nominated finalists have been announced since 1980).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board selection and override rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The board selects the winner by majority vote from the nominations, or bypasses the nominations and selects a different entry following a 75 percent majority vote. The board can also vote to issue no award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although juries nominate finalists, the Board may choose a different winner only with a 75% vote, or decide to give no prize in a category. Entrants should understand the Board has final decision authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury and board compensation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The board and journalism jurors are not paid for their work; however, jurors in letters, music, and drama receive honoraria for the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation differs by domain; journalism jurors serve unpaid while some letters/music/drama jurors receive honoraria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on claiming 'Pulitzer nominee' status
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone whose work has been submitted is called an entrant. The jury selects a group of nominated finalists and announces them, together with the winner for each category. The Pulitzer Board cautions entrants against claiming to be nominees when their work was only submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those named as nominated finalists (announced since 1980) should say they were 'nominated'; using 'Pulitzer-nominated' to mean merely submitted is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Service category definition and award form
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Service – for a distinguished example of meritorious public service by a newspaper, magazine or news site through the use of its journalistic resources, including the use of stories, editorials, cartoons, photographs, graphics, videos, databases, multimedia or interactive presentations or other visual material. The Public Service award is only given to the winning news organization and is awarded in the form of a gold medal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is considered the 'grand prize' among journalism awards; entries are organizational and may include many types of journalistic tools and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News Reporting category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Breaking News Reporting – for a distinguished example of local, state or national reporting of breaking news that, as quickly as possible, captures events accurately as they occur, and, as time passes, illuminates, provides context and expands upon the initial coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on speed and accuracy initially, then on subsequent context and expansion of coverage as events unfold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative Reporting category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigative Reporting – for a distinguished example of investigative reporting, using any available journalistic tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus is on investigative depth, originality, impact and use of journalistic tools to uncover wrongdoing or important information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory Reporting category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanatory Reporting – for a distinguished example of explanatory reporting that illuminates a significant and complex subject, demonstrating mastery of the subject, lucid writing and clear presentation, using any available journalistic tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated on ability to clarify complex topics: subject mastery, clarity of writing and presentation, and effective use of multimedia/tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Reporting category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Local Reporting – for a distinguished example of reporting on significant issues of local concern, demonstrating originality and community expertise, using any available journalistic tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on local significance, originality, and demonstrated knowledge/connection to community; may use multimedia and other journalistic tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Reporting category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: National Reporting – for a distinguished example of reporting on national affairs, using any available journalistic tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on distinction in reporting about national-level issues, including depth, sourcing, and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Reporting category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: International Reporting – for a distinguished example of reporting on international affairs, using any available journalistic tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses quality of reporting about international events, context, and use of journalistic resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature Writing category definition and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature Writing – for distinguished feature writing giving prime consideration to quality of writing, originality and concision, using any available journalistic tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated primarily on prose quality, originality of approach, and concision; may include multimedia elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commentary category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Commentary – for distinguished commentary, using any available journalistic tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on strength of viewpoint, persuasiveness, clarity, and craft of opinion writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism – for distinguished criticism, using any available journalistic tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses originality, insight, clarity, and authority in critical writing (arts, culture, criticism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Writing category definition and test of excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Writing – for distinguished editorial writing, the test of excellence being clearness of style, moral purpose, sound reasoning, and power to influence public opinion in what the writer conceives to be the right direction, using any available journalistic tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on clarity, ethical intent, reasoning quality, and persuasive impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Cartooning category definition (originality and effectiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Cartooning – for a distinguished cartoon or portfolio of cartoons, characterized by originality, editorial effectiveness, quality of drawing and pictorial effect, published as a still drawing, animation or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include originality, editorial impact, and artistic quality; both still and animated formats may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News Photography category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Breaking News Photography – for a distinguished example of breaking news photography in black and white or color, which may consist of a photograph or photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated on immediacy, significance, composition and power of images capturing breaking events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature Photography category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature Photography – for a distinguished example of feature photography in black and white or color, which may consist of a photograph or photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed for storytelling, composition, visual quality and emotional/interpretive power in feature image work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio Reporting category (added 2020) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio Reporting – category added in 2020; recognizes distinguished audio journalism (e.g., program episodes, podcasts) using journalistic tools in audio form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated on reporting quality, storytelling, clarity, and journalistic standards in audio formats; first prize awarded to an episode of This American Life (example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters, Drama, and Music categories: Biography
rubrics_metrics.description: Biography – for a distinguished biography, autobiography or memoir by an American author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should be distinguished and by an American author; applies to biography/autobiography/memoir forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters, Drama, and Music categories: Drama
rubrics_metrics.description: Drama – for a distinguished play by an American playwright, preferably original in its source and dealing with American life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for original source material and themes connected to American life; judged on distinction as a play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters, Drama, and Music categories: Fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction – for distinguished fiction by an American author, preferably dealing with American life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should be by an American author and is preferably concerned with American life; judged on literary distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Nonfiction category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: General Nonfiction – for a distinguished and appropriately documented book of nonfiction by an American author that is not eligible for consideration in any other category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on distinction and documentation; must not fit other letters categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: History category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: History – for a distinguished and appropriately documented book on the history of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works should focus on U.S. history and be appropriately documented and distinguished scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoir or Autobiography category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoir or Autobiography – for a distinguished and factual memoir or autobiography by an American author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on factuality and distinction in memoir/autobiography by an American author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry – for a distinguished volume of original verse by an American poet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses distinction, originality, and quality of verse by an American poet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pulitzer Prize for Music category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Pulitzer Prize for Music – for distinguished musical composition by an American that has had its first performance or recording in the United States during the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility requires first performance/recording in the U.S. during the year and American authorship; judged on distinction of composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition, membership terms, and selection attention
rubrics_metrics.description: The nineteen-member Pulitzer Prize Board convenes semi-annually and comprises major editors, columnists and media executives plus six members drawn from academia and the arts, including the president of Columbia University, the dean of the Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism and the administrator (ex officio, non-voting). The board elects its own members for three-year terms; members may serve a maximum of three terms. Members are selected with close attention 'given to professional excellence and affiliation, as well as diversity in terms of gender, ethnic background, geographical distribution and size of news organization.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board structure and selection are intended to balance professional excellence and diversity; the president and dean serve as permanent members for their appointment durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board operational authority and separation from Journalism School
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 1975, the board has made all prize decisions; although the administrator's office is housed alongside the Graduate School of Journalism and some administrators have had faculty appointments, the board and administration have been operationally separate from the School since 1950.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board holds final decision-making power independent of the Journalism School's governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of no award and board overrides (historical controversies)
rubrics_metrics.description: The board can issue no award in a category and historically has overruled juries or trustees, sometimes creating controversies (examples provided: years when board/trustees overruled jury recommendations or no award was given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should know that even unanimous jury nominations do not guarantee an award; the Board may withhold or override awards according to Plan of Award rules.
